doc.title: Bill Goodwin interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, May 28, 2025

title: Phil Woods's quote and the covenant with the audience
summary: Jazz as a social, dance music and the shared circle between band and audience.

story.theme_name: Where jazz stands today: young players, rock, and the audience
story.community_name: Playing for the audience: communicating from the bandstand

blocks.x: I’ll close with sort of what you’re talking about. A quote from Phil Woods. He says, “Some couple comes up and says, ‘We were married to ‘Round Trip’ or your music means so much,’ those kinds of comments. Believe me, I’m honored to get prizes and all that, but to have the music mean something to people on that level you can’t buy that man, it ain’t for sale.”

I agree completely. You know when you’re on the bandstand you’re playing sincerely it’s almost like you establish a covenant with the audience where you’re all in it together. And I was as much involved in that, I’m part of the circle, they’re part of the circle, we’re all there together for the, you know if not the same reasons we’re all there together, involved in the same thing. And if you get approval from that, you know it’s good. You’re going to do it anyway but it just makes it better when you’re enjoying it with other people and, well you know it’s a social music. It’s a dance form. It’s the thing that people forget now I think, a lot of the young people. You know you’re supposed to be able to dance to this, even if it’s a weird sort of dance. It should move you to — it should inspire you to want to move. And you know — so I know I like something, I start involuntary movement.
